title: The honey forest
hook: the search party wants to storm Lanka itself, an old bear says no, and then they raid the king's honey
carry: svadharma: do your own part, offer the rest

segments.voice: Yesterday: the return. Arishta sinking, the sky like an ocean, and your line: the Sundara Kanda, the book where hope returns.
screen: `SUNDARA KANDA: THE BOOK WHERE HOPE RETURNS.`

segments.voice: On the way home to Kishkindha, the search party is giddy. Hanuman has found Sita. They've crossed back over the sea. And Prince Angada has a big idea: why go home at all? Why not finish this ourselves? Before the honey and the dancing, an old bear has to stop them from doing a job that isn't theirs.
screen: `THE NEWS, AND A BIG IDEA.` → `WHY NOT FINISH IT OURSELVES?`

segments.voice: Angada's plan sounds brave: go back to Lanka, defeat Ravana, and bring Sita to Rama. Jambavan, the old bear, the eldest of the party, says no. We were sent to find her and to tell Rama. That was our task. The rescue is Rama's, and Sita herself said it in the grove: let Rama come for me. So they turn north. And then, with their own job done, they celebrate. They reach the Madhuvana, King Sugriva's guarded honey forest, and with Angada's permission they fall on it: eating, drinking, dancing, tumbling out of the trees. When the guardian, Dadhimukha, Sugriva's uncle, tries to stop them, they shove him around. He runs to the king, furious. And Sugriva smiles. They'd never dare, he tells Rama, unless they'd succeeded. Sita has been found. Here's the teaching under the comedy. Hindus call it svadharma, your own dharma: the duty that is truly yours, by your place in life and your nature. The Bhagavad Gita says it boldly: better your own dharma, done imperfectly, than someone else's done well. Jambavan knew the monkeys' part was to search and report, and the rescue was Rama's. Many teachers read Hanuman's whole life this way: he does his own part completely, then lays the result at Rama's feet. The Gita calls that karma yoga: do what's yours, and offer the fruit.
screen: `STORM LANKA? JAMBAVAN SAYS NO.` · `THE HONEY FOREST.` · `THEY'D NEVER DARE UNLESS...` · `SVADHARMA: YOUR OWN DUTY.` · then, large: `DO YOUR PART, OFFER THE REST.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and bring to mind one thing that's weighing on you this week. Ask Jambavan's question: which part of this is mine, and which part belongs to someone else? Name your part plainly. Many Hindus finish a task, or a puja, with one word: Krishnarpanam, offered to Krishna. If you pray, say it softly over your part. If you don't, simply breathe out and set the rest down.
The return. Jambavan sends the party home with only its own work done, and Sugriva reads the wrecked honey forest as proof that Sita has been found.
Your line: svadharma, do your own part, offer the rest. Tomorrow, Hanuman stands in front of Rama at last. See you there.

howItsDone: Many Hindus close a task or a puja with the word Krishnarpanam, offered to Krishna, a habit drawn from the Gita's teaching on offering the fruit of action; the Madhuvana raid stays a favorite comic scene in Sundara Kanda recitations.
